title: Judgment on Idolatrous Israel

questions.question: Against what specific geographic feature of Israel is Ezekiel told to set his face and prophesy?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:2 (ESV): "Son of man, set your face toward the mountains of Israel, and prophesy against them,"

questions.question: What does the Lord God say He will bring upon the mountains, hills, ravines, and valleys?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:3 (ESV): "Behold, I, even I, will bring a sword upon you, and I will destroy your high places."

questions.question: What will happen to the high places and the incense altars?
options: They shall be made desolate and broken
They shall be purified by priests
They shall sink into the earth
They will be moved to Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be made desolate and broken
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:4 (ESV): "Your altars shall become desolate, and your incense altars shall be broken,"

questions.question: Where will God cast down the slain of the people of Israel?
options: In the valley of dry bones
At the gates of the temple
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:4 (ESV): "and I will cast down your slain before your idols."

questions.question: What will the Lord God scatter around the altars of Israel?
options: The bones of the people of Israel
The gold and silver of their temples
The leaves of the oak trees
questions.correctAnswer: The bones of the people of Israel
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:5 (ESV): "And I will lay the dead bodies of the people of Israel before their idols, and I will scatter your bones around your altars."

questions.question: What will happen to all the dwelling places in the cities?
options: They will be given to foreigners
They will be filled with wild beasts
They will be burned entirely with fire
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:6 (ESV): "Wherever you dwell, the cities shall be laid waste and the high places ruined,"

questions.question: What is the recurring desired outcome stated throughout Ezekiel when judgment falls? "And you shall..."
options: Know that I am the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: Know that I am the Lord
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:7 (ESV): "And the slain shall fall in your midst, and you shall know that I am the Lord." (This phrase appears over 60 times in Ezekiel).

questions.question: Though God brings destruction, what does He promise will remain among the nations?
options: Some of you who escape the sword
A hidden scroll of the law
questions.correctAnswer: Some of you who escape the sword
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:8 (ESV): "Yet I will leave some of you alive. When you have among the nations some who escape the sword, and when you are scattered through the countries,"

questions.question: What will those who escape remember when they are scattered among the nations?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:9 (ESV): "then those of you who escape will remember me among the nations where they are carried captive,"

questions.question: How did the people of Israel break God's heart, prompting His judgment?
options: By their whorish heart that departed from Him and their eyes that played the whore after their idols
By trusting in the chariots of Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: By their whorish heart that departed from Him and their eyes that played the whore after their idols
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:9 (ESV): "how I have been broken over their whoring heart that has departed from me and over their eyes that go whoring after their idols."

questions.question: What will those who escape do once they remember the Lord and their evil deeds?
options: They will be loathsome in their own sight for the evils that they have committed
They will rise up against Babylon
They will build new altars to the Lord
They will flee to another country
questions.correctAnswer: They will be loathsome in their own sight for the evils that they have committed
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:9 (ESV): "And they will be loathsome in their own sight for the evils that they have committed, for all their abominations."

questions.question: "And they shall know that I am the... I have not said in... that I would do this disaster to them."
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:10 (ESV): "And they shall know that I am the Lord. I have not said in vain that I would do this disaster to them."

questions.question: What physical actions does God command Ezekiel to perform while declaring judgment against the evil abominations of the house of Israel?
options: Clap his hands and stamp his foot
Tear his clothes and put ash on his head
Lift up his voice and weep
questions.correctAnswer: Clap his hands and stamp his foot
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:11 (ESV): "Thus says the Lord God: 'Clap your hands and stamp your foot and say, Alas, because of all the evil abominations of the house of Israel..."'"

questions.question: How will the people perish who are far off, who are near, and who are left and preserved?
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:12 (ESV): "He who is far off shall die of pestilence, and he who is near shall fall by the sword, and he who is left and is preserved shall die of famine. Thus I will spend my fury upon them."

questions.question: Where will the dead bodies of the slain specifically be found, illustrating their idolatry?
options: On every high hill, on all the mountaintops, under every green tree, and under every leafy oak
In the temple courts and the holy of holies
In the valley of Hinnom and the valley of Jehoshaphat
At the gates of the city and the doors of their houses
questions.correctAnswer: On every high hill, on all the mountaintops, under every green tree, and under every leafy oak
questions.explanation: Ezekiel 6:13 (ESV): "when their slain lie among their idols around their altars, on every high hill, on all the mountaintops, under every green tree, and under every leafy oak—wherever they offered pleasing odor to all their idols."

key_verse_text: "And the slain shall fall in your midst, and you shall know that I am the Lord."
